response.justification: Broad, deep engineering background (14+ years) with genuine high-throughput experience at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (micro-services handling millions of HTTP requests per second, low-latency async I/O), current Staff-level title, and directly relevant hands-on work with agentic tooling (MCP code generators, AI-agent infrastructure) — which maps well to the AI-native mindset requirement. However, the resume shows no Python at all despite it being a must-have core language, and the bulk of recent work is full-stack product engineering (TypeScript/Node, React, MongoDB) rather than large-scale distributed systems design or technical strategy ownership. Stakeholder management, on-call/operational ownership, and cross-functional influence are not evidenced explicitly. Worth a screen to probe Python depth and distributed-systems ownership, but not a clear yes on paper.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency micro-services experience (millions of req/sec)
Hands-on agentic/AI tooling work incl. MCP code generators and dev tooling
Strong engineering craft: TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based dev, open-source test frameworks, teaching/talks
concerns: No Python listed anywhere; core must-have language unproven
Recent roles skew full-stack product work over distributed-systems architecture
Little evidence of technical strategy, stakeholder management, or on-call/incident ownership
